newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts trade surplus to Jan 28 - source.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts trade surplus to Jan 28 - source.

text.p: Brazil was posting a $220 million trade surplus with exports of $3.13 billion and imports of $2.91 billion up to January 28, according to internal government documents made available to Reuters.
The documents showed that average daily imports in the first week of the month were a miserly $3.3 million, picking up gradually to average $153.1 million by January 28.

Average daily exports by January 28 were $164.8 million. The Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper said Friday the unexpected trade surplus was due to problems with the new SISCOMEX import registration system.
Officials have also suggested that importers bought extra stocks in December because of anticipated problems with the SISCOMEX system, which came on line January 1.

Neither Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, nor Everardo Maciel, head of the Internal Revenue Service which oversees the SISCOMEX system, were immediately available for comment.
A January surplus would be the first since last May. Brazil posted a record trade gap of $5.54 billion in 1996.
